A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TED2025 study. All 23 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D and extended corpus tables, support reliable textual and visual comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original corpus analyses, continued-pretraining and instruction-tuning experiments, and supplementary evaluations in Sections 3–6 and Appendices A, C and D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the model comparisons in Tables 3–5 and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: TED2025 construction, LoRA-based continued pretraining, and the MT, CLTS, MTC and CLP instruction-tuning procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora and six evaluation benchmarks: MMMLU, XCOPA, FLORES-101, FLORES-200, xIFEval and SIB-200. Language, domain and transfer-scenario coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including Baseline and Unaligned in Tables 3–4 and the instruction-objective variants in Table 5. Figure 6 retains the same with-English and without-English comparison.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, sampling, metrics and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Figure 6 relabels existing results without documenting any experimental-setting change.

E4.justification: Figure 6 revises the reported English-pivot ablation by reversing its condition legend. No new ablations are added; the parallelism, data-size, language-family, domain-transfer and representation analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Run and seed disclosures, uncertainty displays and statistical-testing practices are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E6.justification: Figure 6 reassigns existing scores to the opposite English condition. For Group 1 MMMLU, with/without English changes from 20.84/23.17 in v1 to 23.17/20.84 in v2. The numerical magnitudes and all other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Mathematical content, including Appendix A's combinatorial accounting of parallel tuples and sentences, is unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same corpus contribution, novelty positioning and claims about multilingual adaptation, instruction tuning and generalization.

C2.justification: The explanations of English's task-dependent role and other mechanisms are unchanged. Limitations concerning LoRA-only training, corpus scale and domain transfer are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same hyperparameters, hardware, training and inference tools, and prompt sources. Code-access information and instruction templates are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions, citations, bibliography and positioning relative to earlier parallel corpora and multilingual adaptation methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Ge Gao and the Minzu University of China affiliation to the first page and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 changes its legend from hatched=with English and plain=without English to the reverse, with small typography and annotation-placement adjustments. The first-page author block expands; other figures, tables and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Figure 6's reversed English-condition legend, bringing its main trends into agreement with Section 5.2. This resolves a misleading presentation of a supporting ablation and improves internal consistency. The remaining scientific content and limitations are unchanged.
